text: STPGC extends graph strong collapse and graph edge collapse from algebraic topology into scalable graph coarsening algorithms, including GStrongCollapse, GEdgeCollapse, and NeighborhoodConing (Section 3.1, Section 3.2, Section 3.3).
Lemma 2.5 proves that graph strong collapse and graph edge collapse operations preserve homotopy equivalence of the underlying graph (Section 2.2, Lemma 2.5).

GStrongCollapse and NeighborhoodConing provably do not increase shortest-path distances, while GEdgeCollapse increases shortest paths by at most 1 per removed edge (Section 3.4, Lemma 3.3, Lemma 3.4).

On DBLP at coarsening ratio c=0.1, STPGC runs in 6.37s versus 100.42s for GEC, a 15.7x speedup, while achieving higher downstream node-classification accuracy (82.4-84.6% vs 78.9-82.9%) (Table 1, Table 2, Section 4).

On the cit-Patent dataset, STPGC achieves up to 37x runtime acceleration over GEC while demonstrating near-linear scalability across LiveJournal, YouTube, cit-Patent, and Flixster (Figures 7-8, Section 4).
STPGC strictly preserves 1-Betti numbers throughout the ExactCoarsening phase, unlike competing methods that show immediate topological degradation (Figure 4, Section 4).
